Class: a principle gap between the protocol text and its landed reader — the skills seat's topic.

Dedupe words: `dead-claim reclaim Release different author` · `CLAIM_RETRACTION_RULE same author` · `C9 hand-over stood-down session` · `Release on the holder's behalf` · `claude[bot] retired identity retraction`. Dedupe reading at filing: the lane's 28 open cards and the 37 open `finding` cards in objectstack, matched on `Release` / `retract` / `dead` / `reclaim` / `hand-over` — no hit (#18773, the retraction-spelling card, is about WHICH spellings count, not WHOSE).

## One sentence

The protocol has one act that takes a dead claim off a card — the reclaiming seat's `Release:` with cause (SKILL.md :496) — and the landed reader refuses to see it: a `Release:` retracts only its **own author's** older claims (`check-clause2-carriers.mjs` :1714 `CLAIM_RETRACTION_RULE`, 「⛔ never a DIFFERENT author's line」), and the C9 remedy adds 「⛔ never a `Release:` on the holder's behalf」; so a card whose claimant's login is gone (a stood-down session, a retired identity, a silent human) can never be re-claimed without a judged C9 red, and the ruling's twelve reconciliation releases retracted nothing.

## The two texts

- SKILL.md :488 「死认领回收:认领 >~24h ⇒ 疑死 …」 and :496 「再评论询问,静默一窗后释放回队(`Release:` 行载因)」 — the reclaimer writes the release.
- `scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs` :1714 `CLAIM_RETRACTION_RULE` — 「A claim LEAVES the pool when a LATER comment BY THE SAME AUTHOR retracts it … ⛔ never a DIFFERENT author's line」; `claimRetractions` implements exactly that (`candidate.author !== claim.author` ⇒ skip).
- The same file's C9 remedy sentence (:2078, the `claimHandovers` doc block): 「the TAKER posts nothing until then: no work under a claim the holder has not released, ⛔ never a second `Claim:`, ⛔ never a `Release:` on the holder's behalf」; design note 4 (:2037) says the retired identity is 「an author like any other」 and its dead-claim `Release:` is 「the seat's act, ⛔ not a special case in the reader」 — which is the gap stated as a feature: the reader has no way to register that act.
- `CROSS_AUTHOR_CLAIM_ROW_EFFECTIVE_AT` (:2056) = 2026-09-19T03:45Z: any `Claim:` after that instant by a login other than the last live claimant's is judged (exit 4 on `--pair`, a red row in the sweep) unless the earlier claim was retracted by its own login.

## Instances read this shift (all with `--pair` / thread reads at 2026-09-20T03:02Z)

|---|---|---|---|
| objectui#9370 → PR objectui#9378 | `os-tesla` 5652138683 (the `domain:ui` seat's dispatch, session stood down) · `os-justin` 5689310818 (branch-line recovery, session `session_01XeoGH6X7MtfbjcRDscyXi1`, stood down) | only a comment from the `os-justin` login | the skills seat, which the reconciliation ask (5739015009) named as the taker after one silent working day, cannot post a `Claim:` without a judged red; it takes the review and the Tier H terminal as the lane's reviewing seat WITHOUT a claim, and the card's `pm:dispatched`-without-assignee half-state can only be healed by the label swap at the terminal |
| objectstack-ai/objectui#10102 | `hotlong` 5486688759 (maintainer; branch on neither `origin`, no PR, silent through the window) · `claude[bot]` 5552047289 (retired) | `hotlong` alone; `claude[bot]` never | the seat's promised 「records its release」 cannot be written as a `Release:` line without breaking the stricter rule; the card stays free by shape (`pm:queue`, no assignee) with a standing claim nobody can clear |
| the ruling's five `claude[bot]` pairs (#13503, objectstack-ai/objectui#10102, objectui#4730, objectstack-ai/objectstack#7848, objectstack-ai/objectstack#7924 …) | the retired identity | nobody | the seat's dead-claim `Release:` lines posted 2026-09-19T03:31Z are prose to the reader; listed C9-BEFORE-EFFECTIVE forever (harmless only because they pre-date the instant) |

## What is asked (a text-and-reader change, one PR, `scripts/pm/**` + SKILL.md; the shape is the dev's with the evidence above)

- Decide the one sanctioned spelling for a dead-claim reclaim by a different login — e.g. a `Release:` line that names the retracted claim's comment id or session and carries a cause — and make `claimRetractions` accept exactly that spelling from a different author when the named claim is older and its author has no later comment (fail closed otherwise); keep 「never a bare different-author Release」 for live holders.
- Or, if the ruling is that no other login may ever retract, say so in SKILL.md :496 and give the dead-claim route a different act (e.g. the lane seat's take under a named rule) that C9 does not judge — and say which seat lands a stood-down dispatch's PR.
- Either way: the reader's self-test pins the chosen spelling from both sides (accepted from the reclaimer, refused from a bystander), the C9 remedy sentence names it, and the two texts agree.
